classification.difficultyReason: Combine midpoint and perpendicular-gradient calculations to find two bisectors, then solve their equations simultaneously.

content.prompt: $A(0,4)$, $B(4,0)$ and $C(0,-4)$ are the vertices of triangle $ABC$.

spec.description: Axes with arrowheads and no ticks or grid; A and C lie on the y-axis and B on the positive x-axis. Segments AB and BC complete the triangle with AC coincident with the y-axis. Ordinary source blue segments and red point markers become black under house style; the origin label is omitted under the graph convention.
spec.mathematics: A=(0,4), B=(4,0), C=(0,-4); AB has gradient -1 and BC has gradient 1.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied vertices and sides are visible; no bisectors or calculated midpoints are shown.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the equation of the perpendicular bisector of interval:

answer.worked:
The perpendicular bisector passes through the midpoint of $AB$.

$$\begin{align*}M_{AB}&=\left(\frac{0+4}{2},\frac{4+0}{2}\right)\\M_{AB}&=(2,2)\\m_{AB}&=\frac{0-4}{4-0}\\m_{AB}&=-1\end{align*}$$

The perpendicular gradient is $1$.

$$\begin{align*}y-2&=1(x-2)\\y&=x\end{align*}$$

The perpendicular bisector passes through the midpoint of $BC$.

$$\begin{align*}M_{BC}&=\left(\frac{4+0}{2},\frac{0+(-4)}{2}\right)\\M_{BC}&=(2,-2)\\m_{BC}&=\frac{-4-0}{0-4}\\m_{BC}&=1\end{align*}$$

The perpendicular gradient is $-1$.

$$\begin{align*}y+2&=-1(x-2)\\y&=-x\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the coordinates of the intersection of the two perpendicular bisectors found in part a.

answer.worked:
At the intersection, $y=x$ and $y=-x$.

$$\begin{align*}x&=-x\\2x&=0\\x&=0\\y&=0\end{align*}$$

The intersection is $(0,0)$, which satisfies both equations.
